source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-302842:Nautiluses and zombie nautiluses never despawn
source_meta._title: Zombie nautiluses generated in ocean ruins are not persistent

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.11 Release Candidate 2 in a newly created singleplayer world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode with commands enabled, a non-Peaceful difficulty such as the default Normal difficulty, and a render distance of at least 8 chunks.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.11 Release Candidate 2. Do not use the fix version, 1.21.11 Release Candidate 3.
Use a newly created world so the target ocean-ruin chunks have not already been generated or visited in this save.
Enable commands for the world. Creative mode is recommended so the player can safely remain underwater and use all required teleport commands without Survival hazards interfering.
Set Render Distance to 8 chunks or greater before generating the target area.
Do not name, mount, leash, place in a boat, or otherwise interact with the target zombie nautilus, because such actions could change its persistence or behavior.
Keep the world difficulty above Peaceful so hostile mobs are not removed for an unrelated reason.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition using the installation for version 1.21.11 Release Candidate 2, then wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left version label on the main menu identifies the running version as 1.21.11 Release Candidate 2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and ensure commands are enabled. Open the world-generation settings, enter the report's seed exactly, and create the world.
steps.success_cue: A new Creative singleplayer world opens and the player can move normally.

steps.action: Confirm that the difficulty is not Peaceful. If necessary, press Esc, select Options, open Difficulty, and choose Normal or another non-Peaceful difficulty.
steps.success_cue: The active difficulty is Easy, Normal, or Hard rather than Peaceful.

steps.action: Set the render distance to at least 8 chunks: press Esc, select Options, select Video Settings, adjust Render Distance to 8 chunks or greater, and select Done until returning to the world.
steps.success_cue: The Video Settings screen shows Render Distance set to 8 chunks or greater, and the player has returned to gameplay.

steps.action: Wait before teleporting until the initial spawn terrain has rendered and movement and commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby chunks are visible, the loading screen is gone, and player movement responds without world-loading pauses.

steps.action: Teleport to the report's target coordinates. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The teleport completes and the player is at approximately X=-9591, Y=63, Z=8825. Ocean terrain begins rendering around the destination.

steps.action: Do not issue another command yet. Wait until the destination chunks, including the nearby ocean-ruin area, have rendered and player movement and commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding ocean terrain is loaded, no terrain-loading screen remains, and the player can move normally at the destination.

steps.action: Locate the nearest generated zombie nautilus using the report's selector. Press T, enter the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command teleports the player to a zombie nautilus associated with the ocean-ruin area. If the command instead reports that no entity was found, the required setup state was not reached; stop and retry in another newly created world using the same version, seed, settings, and sequence.

steps.action: Allow the immediate surroundings at the zombie nautilus to finish rendering. Do not interact with, name, mount, attack, or otherwise modify the zombie nautilus.
steps.success_cue: The player is beside the zombie nautilus, the nearby ocean-ruin terrain is loaded, and the entity has not been altered by player interaction.

steps.action: Teleport vertically to absolute Y=256 while retaining the current X and Z coordinates. Press T, enter the report's command exactly, and press Enter. The number 256 is an absolute Y coordinate because it does not have a tilde; do not change this to /tp ~ ~256 ~.
steps.success_cue: The teleport completes. The player remains at the same horizontal X and Z location and is now at approximately Y=256.

steps.action: Wait until the high-altitude teleport has completed and movement and commands respond normally before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The player is stable at approximately Y=256, the loading transition is finished, and chat commands can be entered normally.

steps.action: Teleport back to absolute Y=64 at the same X and Z coordinates. Press T, enter the report's command exactly, and press Enter. The number 64 is an absolute Y coordinate; do not change this to a relative vertical movement.
steps.success_cue: The teleport completes. The player is at approximately Y=64 at the same horizontal location, and the surrounding ocean chunks have rendered enough for commands to respond normally.

steps.action: Run the nearest-zombie-nautilus teleport command a second time. Press T, enter the command exactly with its leading slash, press Enter once, and immediately hand control to the observation subsystem without issuing additional commands.
steps.success_cue: The second nearest-zombie-nautilus command has been submitted, and its resulting chat response and any resulting player teleport are available for the observation subsystem to inspect.

stor.handoff_condition: The second `/tp @n[type=zombie_nautilus]` command has just been submitted after the player moved from the ocean ruin to absolute Y=256 and back to absolute Y=64. Begin observing the command response and player destination immediately, without performing another action.
uncertainties: A report comment states that one tester did not find a zombie nautilus at the primary coordinates and instead found one near /tp -7326 46 6539; the main report's seed and coordinates remain the primary reproduction path and the alternate location has not been substituted.

The report does not explicitly state game mode or difficulty. Creative mode, commands enabled, and a non-Peaceful difficulty are practical setup choices intended to execute the supplied commands safely without removing the target for an unrelated reason.
The report says render distance 8 or more but does not specify simulation distance, so no simulation-distance requirement has been added.

If the first `/tp @n[type=zombie_nautilus]` lookup fails, the subsequent steps do not establish this report's required precondition. A fresh world retry is preferred over continuing or manually summoning a replacement, because the bug specifically concerns a zombie nautilus generated as part of an ocean ruin.
